reason: The Hebrew text contains explicit statements that God intends to preserve and sustain Jacob's family. In Genesis 45:5-8, Joseph tells his brothers that God ('Elohim') sent him to Egypt 'to preserve life' (לְהַחֲיוֹת) and to establish them as 'a great escape' during the famine. The narrative demonstrates this divine intention through Joseph's actions—providing grain during the famine, settling them in the best land (Goshen), and sustaining them with food. Joseph's interpretation of events explicitly attributes his position and his family's salvation to God's plan: 'וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם לָכֶ֛ם שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּלְהַחֲיוֹ֣ת לָכֶ֔ם לִפְלֵיטָ֖ה גְּדֹלָֽה' ('God sent me before you to establish you as a remnant in the land and to preserve you as a great escape'). The text thus presents God's will as oriented toward the welfare and survival of the Hebrew people.
